title: Supervisor Coach: Gas terminal release and fire, 2020
audience: First-line supervision (T2): maintenance, instrument and operations supervisors and shift in-charges
status: Learning purposes: not a statutory document. Derived from a ProbeMatrix investigation export; learnings are evidence-linked but should be validated by the organisation before adoption. Draft learnings: the investigation status is in progress.

incident.title: Hazira gas terminal condensate release and fire

data_quality.text: Draft learnings from an unreviewed analysis: the export's investigation status is in progress and no finding is marked as edited by a person. Validate every item before adoption.

bottom_line.text: No specification, no start; no recorded test, no hand-back: the seal job ran without either, and the seal it fitted is the probable release source.
A substitute part that has become regular practice is still a change: ask for the change review before you authorise it.
Close the loop: a notification left open and a repeat repair left unescalated took away the last checks before the release.
On the night, isolation waited for escalation; supervisors need written criteria and authority to isolate, which the site has still to settle.
Put each check on the form where the work is released, so it becomes the easy way rather than a reminder.

items.when: before a pressure-boundary job is released
items.text: The part to be fitted matches a written specification for that item. No specification on file means the job waits until one is found or an approved substitute is recorded.

items.when: before any substitute or not-in-kind part is fitted
items.text: A part, material or size different from the original carries a management-of-change number. A substitute chosen as regular practice is still a change.

items.when: before work on hydrocarbon equipment starts
items.text: A work permit and a job safety plan are in place for the task. A maintenance notification is not a permit.

items.when: when planning a job that opens a pressure boundary
items.text: A second person other than the fitter is named to check the part, the method and the test.
Someone on the crew knows the item's specification and the test the joint needs, or the job waits for technical support.
The item's history is read before the job. A third repair on the same item goes to a root-cause review, not to another identical fix.

items.when: before calibration of a critical high-pressure meter
items.text: A checklist with as-found and as-left values and a change log is issued with the job.

items.when: before an isolation is planned from a drawing
items.text: The drawing is a controlled, approved copy that matches the valves and meters in the field; a mismatch is reported before the plan is used.

items.group: Make the safe way the easy way
items.when: before equipment returns to service after pressure-boundary work
items.text: A recorded test to the written test pressure, with the witness's signature, is attached to the job. Operating pressure alone does not prove the joint.

items.when: before equipment returns to service after pressure-boundary work
items.text: The record shows the specification reference of the part fitted.
The maintenance notification is closed with what was found, what was done and how it was tested, and the closure is reviewed.
The work permit is closed and returned, and any missing permit is followed up.

items.when: before a calibration record is signed
items.text: Every setting changed during the job, including one changed back, is on the record with as-found and as-left values.

items.group: Make the safe way the easy way
items.when: before operations take the equipment back
items.text: Operations accept the equipment in writing, against the test record, rather than by putting it back on line.

A repeat is a signal, not a routine. The same meter had its gasket changed three times in about 22 months, each time with the same substitute part, and none of the repairs was escalated for root cause. When the same item comes back a third time, raise a root-cause request with the maintenance planner and tell the engineering function, and do not accept the same fix again without that review.

An inspection result needs a decision, not a coat of paint. Pitting and wall loss found on a zero-corrosion-allowance line in July 2019 were painted, with no review of whether painting was enough. When an inspection reports wall loss or pitting, send it to the integrity engineers for a fitness-for-service decision before the coating work is accepted.

A defect on standby equipment matters most when it is needed. Two of four diesel fire-water pumps were under maintenance and one tripped after about two minutes, with no cause found or action recorded. Record a trip or failed start the same shift, raise it as a safety-critical defect, and escalate to the fire-protection owner when a pump stays unavailable.

sections.heading: In an emergency
sections.intro: The findings show isolation delayed while the response escalated. These are questions for the site to settle, not authority supervisors already hold.

items.to: Plant leadership (owner of the emergency plan)
items.question: On a confirmed major hydrocarbon release, who on shift may isolate without calling up the chain, and on what criteria?
items.why: The on-site plan named hydrocarbon leakage but gave no isolation criteria, and isolation authority was not allocated to the on-shift crew; the response escalated by phone while the cloud grew.
items.good_evidence: Written isolation criteria and delegated authority for each release scenario, known to every shift and tested in a night-shift drill.

items.question: Which valves isolate each section of the unit, and from where can they be worked if the area cannot be entered?
items.why: The emergency valves could only be closed by hand at the valve, and the release made the area unreachable.
items.good_evidence: An isolation matrix for each area at the control-room console, showing which valves are local-only and the plan when access is denied.

items.to: Operations function, with the security function
items.question: Should the shift treat any outside report of vapour or noise as a confirmed release until it is proved otherwise?
items.why: The control room heard of the release as "some vapour cloud or steam leakage", after it had been relayed and re-described.
items.good_evidence: A standing instruction and a standard release message, used in joint security and operations drills.

items.question: Who on each shift is qualified and practised to lead an emergency isolation?
items.why: Control-room staff held emergency duties after general training only, with no defined qualification or simulator practice.
items.good_evidence: A defined control-room qualification used as a rostering rule, with a record per shift.

items.group: Make the safe way the easy way
items.when: when pressure-boundary work is handed back without a test record
items.text: Decline to accept the equipment until the test record and the witness's signature are attached. Expect management to back the delay.

items.group: Make the safe way the easy way
items.when: when the only seal on offer has no specification
items.text: Decline to start the job. Expect the engineering function to provide a specification or an approved substitute.

items.when: when hazardous work is about to run on a notification only
items.text: Decline to start until the permit and job safety plan are issued.

items.when: when a crew member without emergency-isolation practice would be alone on emergency duty
items.text: Decline the roster and ask for a qualified person on the shift. Expect the roster to change, not the risk to be accepted.

items.when: when a calibration record arrives without a checklist or with a setting change left out
items.text: Decline to sign it until the checklist and every change are recorded.

Stop work and the right to warn. Some regimes give workers and supervisors a right to stop work or to warn of imminent danger. For this run's jurisdiction (India), the coach's jurisdiction notes list the OSH Code 2020 and the Factories Act 1948, and name Factories Act s.41H (content unverified); the site should confirm which apply and how a refusal is supported. The findings show a steep authority gradient and a substitute practice that had become normal, so a refusal will need visible backing from management. This note states no legal conclusion.

sections.heading: Recommendations and how supervisors will know they are working

items.change: Configure the work-order system so a pressure-boundary job cannot be closed, or the equipment released to operations, until a test result and the witness's name are entered.
items.indicator: % of pressure-boundary jobs on the shift log released with a recorded test result and witness

items.change: Link equipment status to notification status, so equipment cannot be set available while its corrective notification is open.
items.indicator: Equipment in service with an open corrective notification, counted at each shift handover

items.change: Add a safety-critical maintenance category to work planning that adds inspection, test-witness and close-out review steps by itself.
items.indicator: % of safety-critical jobs on the shift record with every verification step signed by someone other than the performer

items.change: Set a repeat-failure trigger in the maintenance system that opens a root-cause task when the same item needs a set number of corrective jobs within a set period (the maintenance function sets the numbers).
items.indicator: Repeat repairs on the same tag escalated for root cause, counted from the shift records

items.change: Make the electronic permit mandatory for hydrocarbon work, with the job safety plan attached, and reconcile issued and closed permits every day.
items.indicator: Permits issued but not reconciled at the end of each shift

items.change: Issue calibration checklists for high-pressure meters with as-found and as-left values and a change log, verified by a second person.
items.why_not_stronger: A calibration management system that records configuration changes by itself is the stronger control and is in the Learnings Register; the checklist is the step a supervisor can put in place on the next job while that is decided.

lint_ok.reason: The checklist is the supervision-level system fix for an L3 checking gap; the engineering option is named in why_not_stronger.

items.indicator: % of critical calibrations on the shift record with a complete checklist and second-person check

items.situation: A fitter tells you the high-pressure meter is ready to box up. The original seal is not in stores, so the crew used the O-ring they always use. Operations want the meter back on line in the morning, and nobody can tell you the test pressure.
prompts: What do you check before you sign the job?
What do you say to operations about the morning?
Who do you call for the specification and the test pressure?
How do you make sure the next crew does not face the same choice?

items.situation: A notification comes in for a meter malfunction. Looking at the history, you see the same meter's gasket has been changed twice before in under two years, and the last notification for it was never closed.
prompts: Is this a repair job or a reliability problem?
Who do you escalate it to, and what do you ask for?
What would you want closed before this job starts?

items.situation: At night the control room gets a call about "some vapour cloud or steam leakage" near the metering area. The gas alarm sounds a moment later. Your engineers go out and come back saying they cannot get near the source.
prompts: What is your first decision, and who makes it?
Which valves would isolate the release, and can anyone reach them?
Whom do you call, and while you wait, what do you do?
What would you want the emergency plan to have told you?

rows: Fit only the seal the specification calls for
Any pressure part on the unit with no specification the crew can find
Job card: a specification reference field that must be filled before release
Prove the joint before it goes back into service
Jobs where the crew could not name the test pressure
Return-to-service certificate: test result, test pressure and witness
Ask for the second check on a high-consequence job
Jobs the crew thinks need a second check and do not get one
Job card: a named checker for safety-critical jobs
Say so when you are fixing the same fault again
Items the crew keeps repairing
Job card: a repeat-failure box that starts a root-cause request
A gas alarm is late news
Alarms the crew is unsure trip anything
Shift log: alarm response checked at handover
If you cannot reach the source, think isolation from a distance
Isolation points the crew could not reach in a release
Permit form and shift log: the isolation matrix for the area
Call the control room that can act, and say what you see
Who the security posts would call, and the words they would use
Shift log: the standard release message, checked in joint drills
A flameproof fitting with a bolt missing is not flameproof
Damaged fittings seen on rounds
Area round sheet: an item-by-item check of flameproof fittings

limits: Management decisions on staffing, budgets, procedures and the emergency plan are for manager-coach and site-leadership-coach; this pack names them only as questions or as the support supervisors should expect.
The card titles in Brief your crew come from frontline-learning-cards for this run.
